title: AZDAST the new horizon in antimicrobial synergism detection
author: Ziaei-Darounkalaei, Ameri, et al.

steps.title: Prepare sterile petri dish
steps.instruction: Obtain a sterile glass petri dish of 12 cm diameter (other sizes may be used if they meet agar‑depth regulations).

steps.title: Make agar adhesive
steps.instruction: Prepare a glue consisting of 1.5 × concentrated Mueller‑Hinton agar that has been autoclaved, then cooled to 44–48 °C; keep the molten agar warm (e.g., on a heater) to prevent solidification.

steps.title: Paste first antibiotic disk
steps.instruction: Dip the first antibiotic paper disk (designated “A”) into the warm agar glue and place it at its predetermined position on the bottom of the petri dish before agar is poured.

steps.title: Paste second antibiotic disk
steps.instruction: Dip the second antibiotic paper disk (designated “B”) into the same agar glue and paste it at its predetermined position(s) on the dish floor, completing the full pattern before agar pouring.

steps.title: Pour agar to fill dish
steps.instruction: Warm 40 mL of autoclaved Mueller‑Hinton broth to ≈46 °C in a shaking water bath for 30 min, then pour it into the dish to obtain an agar depth of 3.5 mm (acceptable range 3–4 mm). Allow the agar to solidify (a few minutes, <4 min).

steps.title: Prepare bacterial suspension
steps.instruction: From a fresh 24‑h culture, prepare a suspension equivalent to a 0.5 McFarland standard (optical density 0.08–0.10 at 625 nm).

steps.title: Inoculate plate
steps.instruction: Using a sterile swab, spread the bacterial suspension uniformly over the solidified agar surface (spread‑plate technique).

steps.title: Incubate plate
steps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated plate at 37 °C for 18 h (observe the “rule of 15,15,15”).

steps.title: Measure inhibition zones
steps.instruction: Measure the diagonal of each zone of inhibition with a ruler or caliper.

steps.title: Interpret synergy
steps.instruction: Compare the measured diameters of single‑disk zones with those of the combined (dual) disks according to Table 1 and the combination‑index grading (CI) scheme.
